writeup: TIC 403030272 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 18.91 days, detected through automated analysis of TESS photometry. The primary eclipse produces an 11.70% dimming, while no secondary eclipse was detected. The eclipse signal shows strong statistical significance with a box least-squares detection value of 518.3 and pixel-level confirmation yielding a peak signal-to-noise ratio of 95.7. However, the eclipse depths alternate significantly between cycles in a way that suggests the true period is twice the initial measurement, which automated quality checks flagged. The target does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs, making it a novel candidate. The automated screening model assigned it a confidence score of 0.63 on a scale where higher values indicate greater likelihood of being a genuine eclipsing system.
